home.learnBody: A five-minute guide to spotting a scam call, your legal rights, and exactly what to do in the first hour.

guide.title: Stay Safe
guide.subtitle: How to recognise a scam, your rights, and what to do — in your language.

two.title: Five words that end any scam

four.title: If it happens: the first hour

c1.intro: It starts like any other evening. The phone rings. The voice on the other end sounds official, urgent, and certain.

dialogue.scammer1: Namaste, I am Inspector Sharma from the CBI, Delhi. A parcel in your name was caught at Mumbai customs. It contained drugs. You are now under 'digital arrest'.
dialogue.raju1: What? Me? I don't know anything about this... I only...
dialogue.scammer2: Tell no one. This is a sub-judice matter. Keep your camera on. We will investigate you fully. Then you must transfer 3 lakh rupees to a 'safe RBI account'.

c1.keyFactHeadline: "Digital arrest" does not exist in Indian law.

facts.loss: ₹22,495 crore was lost to cyber fraud in 2025.
facts.targets: Favourite targets: people over 50, retired professionals, and government employees.
facts.arc: The scam always follows four steps: Authority → Accusation → Isolation → Money demand.

c2.intro: This time, Raju uncle has Kavach on his phone. The confidence meter climbs. The warning appears. He reads it, and looks back at the caller — calm.
c2.rajuAfter: He calls his son. He hangs up. The fake police station falls apart.
c2.fiveWordsIntro: Remember five words. They end any scam call instantly.
c2.signsIntro: Six signs it is a scam

s1.title: They demand secrecy
s1.quote: "Don't tell your family. This is confidential."
s1.detail: Real investigations involve your lawyer, not secrecy.

s2.title: They demand money on the call
s2.detail: No government body collects money over a phone call. Ever.

s3.title: They keep you on video all day
s3.detail: No legal process requires continuous video surveillance from your home.

s4.title: They use fear to stop you thinking
s4.quote: "You will be arrested in one hour."
s4.detail: Pressure and urgency are tools, not law.

s5.title: The number looks Indian but sounds foreign
s5.detail: Report it via Chakshu at sancharsaathi.gov.in.

s6.title: They already know your name and Aadhaar
s6.detail: Your Aadhaar number is widely available. It proves nothing.

c3.intro: Priya, a lawyer, explains the rights that dismantle the scam's premise. A citizen who knows these cannot be trapped.

r1.title: There is no such thing as "digital arrest"
r1.body: The Supreme Court of India confirmed in 2025 that "digital arrest" has no legal basis under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, or any Indian law. A police officer cannot arrest you over a video call. A summons under Section 63 BNSS must be encrypted, digitally signed, and bear a court seal — it is never served by a phone call.
r1.source: Supreme Court of India, Digital Arrest Suo Moto Case (2025)

r2.title: No government body collects money by phone
r2.body: No CBI, ED, TRAI, RBI, Customs, or court collects money via UPI, bank transfer, or WhatsApp. Any such demand is fraud. Impersonating a public servant is an offence under Sections 204 and 205 of the BNS, punishable by up to two years' imprisonment.

r3.title: The 1-hour "golden hour" for recovery
r3.body: If you have transferred money, calling 1930 within 1–2 hours can freeze the destination account before the money is withdrawn. The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) connects 85+ banks and payment intermediaries. More than ₹7,130 crore has been saved through prompt 1930 reporting.
r3.source: Ministry of Home Affairs, Lok Sabha, December 2025

r4.title: Zero liability if reported within 3 days
r4.body: Under the RBI circular of 6 July 2017, if an unauthorised transaction occurs and you report it to your bank within 3 working days, your liability is zero — the bank must refund you. Between 4–7 days: limited liability (₹5,000–₹25,000 cap). After 7 days: you bear the loss. Time is everything.

r5.title: You can file an FIR anywhere in India
r5.body: Cybercrime has pan-India jurisdiction under the IT Act. Under Section 154 BNSS (Zero FIR), any police station must register your complaint regardless of where the crime occurred. For losses above ₹10 lakh, complaints to 1930/NCRP automatically generate a Zero FIR with the e-Crime Police Station, Delhi.
r5.source: IT Act 2000; BNSS 2023, Section 154; MHA e-Zero FIR initiative, May 2025

r6.title: The banking ombudsman is your escalation
r6.body: If your bank refuses to help, file a complaint with the RBI Ombudsman. Banks must respond within 10 working days of a fraud complaint. The RBI can direct banks to refund unauthorised debits.

c4.intro: The exact sequence for the 60 minutes after a fraud. Every minute saved increases the chance of recovery.

s1.title: Call 1930
s1.body: 1930 is India's national cyber-fraud helpline, run 24/7 by I4C (Ministry of Home Affairs). Tell the operator your name, your bank, the amount, when it happened, and the destination UPI or account if you know it. The operator coordinates with your bank and the destination bank to freeze the account. This is the golden hour — every minute matters.

s2.title: Call your bank
s2.body: Call your bank's 24/7 fraud helpline immediately. Say: "Unauthorised UPI transaction, please freeze my account." Get a written or SMS reference number — this is your evidence trail.

s3.title: File on NCRP
s3.body: Go to cybercrime.gov.in and click "Report Financial Fraud". You will need the fraudster's phone/UPI/account, the amount, the date and time, and your transaction screenshot. You receive a complaint ID — save it and share it with your bank. Or open Kavach and tap "Report to 1930" — the form is pre-filled from the call.

s4.title: Report the number to Chakshu
s4.body: Go to sancharsaathi.gov.in/sfc/ and report the fraud number under "Chakshu — Report Suspected Fraud Communication". Select "Impersonation as government official". DoT can block the number across all telecom networks. Report international spoofed numbers via the RICWIN module on the same portal.

after.a1: Follow up with your bank every 48 hours until it is resolved — do not wait passively.
after.a2: If police are unresponsive, escalate to the Superintendent of Police (SP) cyber cell in your district.
after.a3: If the bank refuses to refund, file with the RBI Ombudsman at cms.rbi.org.in.
after.a4: Keep every record: screenshots, bank statements, call logs, and complaint IDs.

remember.title: Remember
remember.r1: Real police never call. They send physical notices.
remember.r2: No government body takes money over the phone.
remember.r3: Call 1930 within 60 minutes. Every minute counts.
remember.r4: You can hang up. You are not in trouble.

c5.shareHint: Send it to your family. One share can protect fifty people.
